title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Crest Album. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every card rebuilds the whole site — picks, grid, standings, admin, auth — not just a skin.

options.label: The Crest Album
options.lineage: Panini crest albums and their numbered die-cut slots
options.thesis: A week is an album page: numbered slots, one per game. An unpicked game is an empty slot with its ghost crest and number printed into the card — so what is still open reads from across the room, before you focus on anything. Refuses the card-grid dashboard and the hairline ledger alike.
options.viewport: A saturated green album sheet. Sixteen numbered slots on a strict grid; empty ones show the ghost crest outline and the fixture number, filled ones carry the crest at full colour. The week rail is the album's page tabs. The open count reads as slots, not as a progress bar: SIX SLOTS EMPTY.
options.risk: Skeuomorphic gloss would read as kitsch and trip your 'must not look vibecoded' constraint. This only works executed as genuine print — die-cut, registration, flat inks — never as drop-shadowed glossy stickers.

raised.raise: One graphic device owns an entire state at full scale. A locked fixture takes a device across the whole slot, never a polite tint.
Four slot states named and visually distinct — empty, placed, revealed-correct, revealed-wrong. 'Not picked' and 'locked' may never blur into each other.
Standings refuse enclosure. Rank reads as foil brightness and scale, not as another table of boxes inside a page already made of boxes.
Total colour commitment. Team colour fills the whole slot band as a flat unmodulated field, never a two-pixel accent stripe.

options.label: Der Tippschein
options.lineage: Kicker Sonderheft tables and the German pools coupon
options.thesis: The week as the ruled coupon this group already knows how to read without instruction. Agate tables, crests set inline at cap height, newsprint that admits it is newsprint, and the tick column as the only interactive element on the page.
options.viewport: One ruled coupon, one line per fixture, tick columns down the right. The whole week fits a single sheet with no scrolling on desktop; the group's standings run as a stub table in the outer column.
options.risk: It is also where most runs land for a German football pool, and it sits close to the ledger you already have. Familiar and genuinely effective — but the least surprising card in this hand.

options.label: The Plate Section
options.lineage: a design annual's plate section on uncoated near-white stock
options.thesis: A season is a plate section: each week a registered plate, crosshairs at every corner, one grotesque carrying display and caption alike, and a single letterpressed seal to prove a person signed it.
options.viewport: One continuous sheet, weeks as registered plates, a sticky bar of mono tokens across the top.
options.case: Holds product clarity outright — a plate section is built for dense reference and hairline division. Loses audience identification: a design annual is not this group's world. This is also the print-system answer to your maximal-Swiss question, warmer and with real press furniture.
options.risk: Closest card to what you already have. The change may land as a refinement rather than a new look.

options.label: Night Instruments
options.lineage: a small aircraft's night instrument six-pack
options.thesis: Outside is ink; inside, a fixed constellation of instruments each owning one truth, read by a practiced cross-check sweep. Your 02:15 Tuesday is literally this scene.
options.viewport: The standings as six gauges in two ranked rows; the live game is the one needle still moving.
options.case: Holds product clarity for the watching-and-settling-up job, and the night scene matches your users exactly. Loses audience identification: sixteen independent binary picks are not a gauge cluster, and the picking page fights the metaphor.
options.risk: Strong for standings, weak for picking — and picking is the job done most often.

options.label: Swiss Utility, Maximal
options.lineage: the world you pinned, pushed to its limit
options.thesis: Keep the ledger and stop being polite about it. Real ink weights instead of hairlines everywhere, a grid hard enough to see, display type at poster scale, and one saturated Swiss red admitted into a system that currently allows no colour of its own.
options.viewport: The pick list under a full-measure red rule, week number set at display scale, scores in numerals large enough to read at arm's length.
options.risk: It is the world you already have. The gain is intensity, not identity — if the goal was a different-looking site, this card will not deliver it.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every pick'em app ships: team-colour gradient headers, same-size fixture cards, a big primary CTA, a progress ring on the week. Executed impeccably rather than ironically.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor already expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from ESPN and DraftKings by design — and the pattern your brief calls 'vibecoded'.
